archetype.name: Rebuilding (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A young, lottery-bound Jazz team that has rebuilt a credible half-court defense around its 2025-26 wreckage, while the offense and the injured frontcourt keep the losses coming.

report.headline: A real defense, a broken offense, and a frontcourt in the trainer's room
report.take:
Utah at 3-15 looks like another year at the bottom, and the record says so: last in the Northwest, 22nd of 30 on the site, and a 12-game losing streak already in the books. The shape of the team has changed, though. Last season's Jazz had a 122.3 defensive rating, 29th in the league. This group sits at 115.9, 19th, and the underlying shot defense is better than that rank: opponents' eFG % is 52.2 (8th), they get to the rim on only 26.7% of their shots (6th), and Utah finishes possessions with a 74.8 DRB % (5th). This is a rebuilding team that can guard people, which these Jazz have not been able to say for three years.

The offense is what sinks it. A 108.7 offensive rating ranks 28th, 5.6 points per 100 possessions below the league, and it is a steep drop from last season's 114.1. Two things drive it. The shooting is below average across the board (TS % 56.2, 24th), and the ball security is poor: a 15.1 TOV %, 26th, against 13.2 a year ago. The usage sits with young guards who are not yet efficient. Keyonte George carries a 28.1 USG % at a passable 56.6 TS %, but Darryn Peterson is at 51.4 on 24.8 usage, and Ace Bailey at 52.8. The backcourt grades D-, and point guards torch Utah at the other end too, with 28.56 points a game allowed to the position (25th).

What the numbers hide is the injury list. Lauri Markkanen, the best-ranked player on the roster by tab rank, has played only 8 games and is out; Jaxson Hayes (67.8 TS %) and Jaren Jackson Jr. are out as well. The frontcourt rotation is now Mo Bamba and whatever is behind him, and Kyle Filipowski's -7.7 BPM shows how thin that is. The record is also a touch worse than the play: W vs Pt Diff is -2, and the margin implies 5 wins rather than 3. That is not a hidden good team, just a bad one losing a couple of extra close games.

The last week was the most encouraging stretch of the season: back-to-back road wins over the Clippers and Lakers, and a +3.4 per-game margin over the last five with only 108.2 points allowed. November's defense was already ahead of October's. Expect the defense to hold up at roughly this level, the offense to tick up when Markkanen returns, and the final record to land in the high teens or low 20s. It is a better process than last year's, without a better ceiling.

strengths.title: Shot defense that actually holds
strengths.body: Utah keeps opponents out of the paint and off the glass: opponents' rim rate ranks 6th, their eFG % 8th, and the defensive rebounding is 5th. It is a structural change from a team that ranked 29th in defensive rating last year, so it is more than a hot month. The catch is that it forces almost nothing, so opponents get plenty of clean possessions and the rating stays mid-pack.

strengths.title: Mo Bamba anchoring the middle
strengths.body: With Hayes out, Bamba is the frontcourt, and he has earned it: a 74.3 TS % on finishes, a 3.2 BPM that leads the roster, and a +6.5 On-Off. He ranks 20th of 92 on the center tab. His usage is low and his efficiency is extreme, so expect some cooling, but his value as the lone healthy big is real.

strengths.title: Small forwards are shut down
strengths.body: Opposing small forwards produce 6.13 fewer points, rebounds and assists combined against Utah than in their other games, the best such mark in the league. Bailey and the wing group have length, and the scheme pushes the action elsewhere. The cost is that the point guards get the ball instead.

concerns.title: An offense that gives possessions away
concerns.body: The 108.7 offensive rating is 28th, and turnovers are a large part of it: the TOV % of 15.1 ranks 26th, up from 13.2 last season. Young guards are carrying heavy usage, and Peterson's 51.4 TS % on 24.8 usage drags the efficiency down. Some of this improves as the rookies settle and Markkanen returns, but it does not reach league average this year.

concerns.title: Frontcourt depth wiped out
concerns.body: Markkanen has played 8 games, and he, Hayes and Jackson Jr. are all listed out. That leaves Bamba and Filipowski, whose -7.7 BPM is the worst on the roster. Until bodies return, any Bamba foul trouble turns the defense's best trait, rim protection, into a liability.

concerns.title: Point guards feast
concerns.body: Opposing point guards average 28.56 points against Utah and score 3.24 above their norms, 27th in the league. That ties directly to a D- backcourt that cannot contain at the point of attack and a defense that forces turnovers less often than almost anyone (27th). The weakness is structural to this guard group.

trend.note: A 1-5 October and a 12-game slide gave way to a better November defense, and the last five games have a +3.4 margin with only 108.2 points allowed. It is a small sample built around two road wins, but the direction is up.

weekAhead.headline: Lakers on the road, then two winnable home tests
weekAhead.body:
The week opens in Los Angeles against a 14-3 Lakers team ranked 3rd on the site, the one Utah just beat 109-97 there on Nov. 18. Repeating it is a tall order. The Lakers lead the league in eFG % and in forcing turnovers, and turnovers are exactly Utah's weakness. Then come two home games against teams with soft defenses: Denver (defense 22nd) and Phoenix (defense 24th), whom Utah lost to by ten at home two days after the Lakers win.

Both home opponents are vulnerable where Utah has some strength. Denver gets torched at the rim and carries an F wing grade, and Phoenix is the worst defensive-rebounding team in the league with a D+ frontcourt. A 1-2 week is the realistic target, and the home pair is where it has to come from.

keyMatchups.title: Utah's turnovers vs Lakers' pressure
keyMatchups.body: The Lakers force turnovers at the league's highest rate, and Utah ranks 26th in protecting the ball. If George and Peterson give the Lakers' top-ranked shooting offense extra possessions, Utah's shot defense won't matter. The Lakers also allow the most points to point guards of nearly anyone, so George has room to score if he stays clean.

keyMatchups.title: Bamba at the rim vs Denver
keyMatchups.body: Denver's opponents shoot 69.2% at the rim, 27th in the league, and Bamba finishes at a 74.3 TS %. Denver also gives up big nights to forwards, 26.47 points to small forwards and 25.73 to power forwards, so Bailey and Sensabaugh should find shots. Denver's A+ backcourt is the danger at the other end.

keyMatchups.title: Second chances against Phoenix
keyMatchups.body: Phoenix's DRB % is the league's worst, and it allows centers 16.33 rebounds a game, also last. Utah's offensive rebounding is only middling, but this is the matchup to crash and manufacture the extra possessions its shooting can't. Phoenix's point guard defense is also last in points allowed.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Utah's guards keep their turnovers down against the Lakers' league-best pressure. If they can, the recent defensive form has a chance to carry over into the two home games.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense looks sustainable: its strengths are shot location and defensive rebounding, which hold up better than forced turnovers or opponents' cold shooting. Expect points allowed to settle around 113-117 a game. The offense has room to grow. Markkanen's return would add a shooter and some efficient usage, and the young guards should cut their turnovers, but nothing here points to a league-average attack. Scoring around 108-112 a game is the realistic band.

The current pace of 14 wins slightly undersells the team, since the margin implies a couple more wins than the record shows and close-game luck tends to even out. A finish of 16-23 wins is our range: an improvement on last season's 22-60 is possible but not likely, and the season remains about development and lottery position rather than the standings.
swingFactors: Turnover rate of George and Peterson
Bamba holding up as the lone healthy big

confidence.note: 18 games in, with three frontcourt players out skewing the picture
